Eagles vs. Bears picks, player props: Expert's best bets for Monday Night Football in NFL Week 3 Philadelphia heads to Chicago on Monday Night Football with the Bears starting Case Keenum at quarterback By Will Brinson Sep 28, 2026 at 8:08 pm ET • 3 min read Add CBS Sports on Google The NFL season really just moves too fast -- it's hard to believe we've almost already shredded through three weeks of football with just the Eagles and Bears left to play in the Week 3 of the season. Bet on Monday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: Ordinarily, this would be a premier primetime game to wrap up the week. It's still possible we get a great game, but the loss of Caleb Williams for this week due to a hamstring injury certainly takes away from the appeal of this one. It is worth noting this line has dipped a point even after the news that Williams would be out for several weeks. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Wager on the NFL with the latest FanDuel promo code and get up to $250 in bonus bets: Best bets for Monday Night Football Eagles -3.5 Road chalk has been BAD so far in Week 3 but I'm not moving off one of my best bets from before the weekend just because of a trend. The Eagles should be able to score at least 24 points against the Bears and I just don't see how Chicago is going to find 20+ points with an offense led by a 38-year-old Case Keenum . Keenum is starting for the Bears this week , even though Tyson Bagent cleared concussion protocol and is available to play. I generally trust Ben Johnson to dial up enough trickeration to keep his team in a game where it doesn't have its star quarterback, but this feels like a terrible matchup. The Eagles are a boring boa constrictor, and that's a bad matchup for an undermanned team in prime time. Monday Night Football player props Case Keenum Over 0.5 interceptions (-122, DraftKings) I think the Bears would, in a perfect world, love to keep Keenum's pass attempts down and just run the heck out of the ball if they could, but neither the Commanders nor Titans were particularly effective on the ground against Philly. As such, I think Keenum's going to have to hoist the ball close to 30 times and that should provide an opportunity for the Eagles to jump a route or find a pick. This price is more than reasonable, especially if Keenum and the Bears are chasing points late. Dontayvion Wicks Over 41.5 receiving yards (-110, DraftKings) Wicks' Eagles career has started off in impressive fashion, with the former Packers receiver producing multiple games north of 70 receiving yards, slotting into the starting lineup for Philly and becoming a trustworthy weapon for Jalen Hurts alongside DeVonta Smith . I like him to clear this number against a Bears defense that has been extremely vulnerable to No. 2 receivers so far this season, at least when the weather's cooperated. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM with promo code CBSSPORTS and get up to $1,500 in bonus bets: Monday Night Football anytime touchdowns Saquon Barkley (-115, DraftKings) I have zero problem laying the juice with the chalky option in Saquon Barkley . The Eagles are not going to try and win this game by slinging the ball everywhere and cutting Hurts loose in the red zone. They're gonna want to pound the ball as much as they can and feed Barkley and maybe even Tank Bigsby (who is a decent price at +650). D'Andre Swift (-105, DraftKings) Nothing too fancy for us here, just some good, old-fashioned cheap touchdown scorers. Swift is priced at +100 and should be Keenum's best friend in this spot, given his ability to catch passes out of the backfield. I also considered Colston Loveland here, but I'm a little worried about the tight end rotation for the Bears. Plus, Swift can score rushing or receiving and should get plenty of action in both facets. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Based on Shough’s age and college profile, there is a possibility the market is overconfident in his abilities. Shough’s season passing total is currently lined within 200 yards of both Justin Herbert and Caleb Williams and 150 yards of Josh Allen , all quarterbacks with more NFL experience and a greater certainty that they will be starting in the league for seasons to come. Last season, Shough played against an extremely favorable slate of opposing defenses. Last year was considered a success for the rookie quarterback, but diving into the numbers raises some question marks for the Saints' passing attack. The Saints faced the 31st-ranked schedule of opposing passing defenses last season and are currently projected to face the 21st-ranked in 2026. In Shough’s nine starts, he faced one single team that finished the season with a winning record. Despite the soft schedule, the Saints dug themselves into early deficits, forcing Kellan Moore into heavier passing scripts. The Saints trailed at halftime in seven of nine games from Week 9 onward. In fact, the Saints led the league with the most offensive snaps while trailing. Although Shough wasn’t a complete garbage time merchant, he averaged 140 passing yards per game in the second half compared to 110 passing yards in the first half. An improved running game could help ease some of the need to rely on Shough as often as last year. The Saints finished 28th in total rushing yards and 31st in yards per rush in 2025 but were aggressive in signing running back Travis Etienne and guard David Edwards to help improve the run game. A better rushing attack can lead to a lower passing rate and create fewer clock stoppages, reducing Shough’s passing yardage ceiling. The Sharp Football season-long projections are more bullish on Shough compared to ESPN, but given the fragility of his profile, there is a good chance that Shough would need to start all 17 games to reach his season-long total. Last season, only 11 quarterbacks started 17 games, which provides a solid argument for betting season-long quarterback unders. In college, Shough did not start more than seven games in any of his first five seasons as he dealt with multiple different season-ending injuries. Betting overs on a sophomore quarterback, who was drafted after six seasons of college football, is probably not optimal. Given Shough’s injury history, there are probably multiple outs to cashing the under. Target Opportunity, Not Just Recent Results Recent box scores only tell part of the story. When evaluating NFL player props, focus on the factors that create opportunities. For quarterbacks, that may include pass attempts, rushing volume and expected game script. For running backs, examine carries, targets, snap share and goal-line work. For receivers and tight ends, prioritize routes run, target share and air yards. A player can fall short of his prop and still have an encouraging role. Conversely, a recent hot streak may be difficult to sustain if it came on limited volume or unusually efficient production. The goal is to project what the player will be asked to do in the upcoming matchup, not simply react to his latest performance. 2. Compare Your Projection With the Best Available Line A player prop becomes attractive when your projection differs meaningfully from the sportsbook’s line. Before placing a wager, compare the listed total with statistical projections, expected game conditions and the probability that the player goes over or under. It is also important to compare lines across multiple sportsbooks. One book might list a receiver at 64.5 yards while another offers 62.5. That difference can determine whether the bet wins or loses. If the totals are identical, compare the odds and select the sportsbook offering the better price. Consistently getting the best number can make a significant difference over an entire NFL season. BettingPros’ odds-shopping guide explains why comparing lines is so important. 3. Establish a dedicated betting bankroll and risk only a small percentage on each wager. BettingPros recommends limiting individual bets to approximately 1% to 5% of your total bankroll. Keep a record of the player, prop, line, odds, stake, result and reasoning behind every bet. Over time, this information can show whether you perform better with certain positions or markets, such as quarterback passing yards, running back rushing attempts or receiver receptions.
